combinations.title: Imports for injecting code into other processes
combinations.explanation: Opening another process, writing to its memory and starting a thread in it is the classic sequence for running code inside a different process.
combinations.limitations: Debuggers, security products, game overlays and accessibility tools use the same functions legitimately. Imports show capability, not use.
combinations.next_step: Find the code that calls these functions and check which processes it targets.

combinations.title: Imports for loading and unprotecting code at run time
combinations.explanation: Resolving functions at run time and changing memory protection are the building blocks of unpacking stubs and in-memory loaders.
combinations.limitations: Many ordinary programs, runtimes and plug-in hosts use both.
combinations.next_step: Check whether the file also shows signs of packing, such as high-entropy executable sections.

combinations.title: Imports for downloading and starting programs
combinations.explanation: Network access combined with starting processes is what a downloader needs to fetch and run further stages.
combinations.limitations: Updaters, installers, browsers and many applications legitimately do both.
combinations.next_step: Look for URLs or host names among the strings and check what is started.

combinations.title: Imports for installing services

attack.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service

combinations.explanation: Installing a service lets a program run at every boot with system privileges.
combinations.limitations: Installers and system administration tools manage services routinely.
combinations.next_step: Look for service names and binary paths among the strings.

combinations.title: Imports for encrypting files while walking the file system
combinations.explanation: Enumerating files and encrypting data is the core capability of ransomware.
combinations.limitations: Backup software, archivers and disk encryption tools need exactly these functions.
combinations.next_step: Look for ransom notes, file extension lists or shadow copy deletion among the strings.

combinations.title: Imports for capturing keyboard input
combinations.explanation: Global hooks and key-state polling can record what a user types in other applications.
combinations.limitations: Games, hotkey utilities and accessibility software use the same functions.
combinations.next_step: Check whether a global hook is installed and where captured data is sent or stored.

combinations.title: Imports for detecting debuggers
combinations.explanation: Programs that check for a debugger may behave differently when analyzed.
combinations.limitations: Debugger checks are common in commercial software, games and runtime libraries.
combinations.next_step: Expect behavior under a debugger to differ and plan dynamic analysis accordingly.

combinations.title: Imports for changing process privileges
combinations.explanation: Enabling privileges or impersonating other users can grant access a program would not normally have.
combinations.limitations: System utilities and installers routinely enable privileges such as shutdown or backup.
combinations.next_step: Check which privileges are requested, for example SeDebugPrivilege among the strings.
